items.followUp: Define one atomic mass unit and write its value in kilograms.

rubric.why: The definition identifies the standard reference atom and fraction used for one atomic mass unit.
rubric.description: Defines 1 u as one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both the one-twelfth fraction and carbon-12 reference.

rubric.why: The numerical value in grams is specifically requested.
rubric.description: Gives the value of 1 u in grams.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 1.66 × 10⁻²⁴ g, allowing equivalent notation.

modelAnswer: One atomic mass unit (u) is one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.

items.followUp: Write the electronic configuration of the chlorine atom, ₁₇Cl, in shells.

rubric.why: The configuration must account for argon’s 18 electrons.
rubric.description: Shows the correct total number of electrons and shell distribution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct shell configuration, 2,8,8.

rubric.why: The requested configuration is the arrangement of electrons in shells.
rubric.description: Writes the shell electronic configuration correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the complete arrangement of 2,8,8.

items.followUp: Describe what happens to an electron when it moves from a higher energy level to a lower one.

rubric.why: Absorption supplies the energy needed for an electron to move to a higher level.
rubric.description: States that an electron absorbs energy to move to a higher energy level.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct absorption and upward-transition relationship.

rubric.why: An electron releases energy when it moves down to a lower energy level.
rubric.description: States that an electron emits energy when it moves to a lower energy level.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct emission and downward-transition relationship.

modelAnswer: An electron absorbs energy when it moves from a lower to a higher energy level.
An electron emits energy when it moves from a higher to a lower energy level.

items.followUp: State the modern periodic law and identify the quantity on which it is based.

rubric.why: The law states that elemental properties recur periodically.
rubric.description: States that the properties of elements are periodic.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the periodic recurrence of properties.

rubric.why: The modern periodic law bases the periodicity on atomic number, not atomic mass.
rubric.description: Identifies atomic number as the basis of the law.

modelAnswer: The properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

items.followUp: How does electron affinity generally change from left to right across a period, and why?

rubric.why: The general trend across a period is an increase in electron affinity.
rubric.description: Gives the general left-to-right trend in electron affinity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electron affinity generally increases across a period.

rubric.why: Increasing nuclear attraction and decreasing atomic size explain the general trend.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable reason for the trend.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating the trend to increasing nuclear charge or decreasing atomic size.

modelAnswer: Electron affinity generally increases from left to right across a period.
This is due to increasing nuclear charge and decreasing atomic size.

items.followUp: Explain how the electronegativity difference between two atoms affects the polarity of their bond.

rubric.why: Unequal attraction for shared electrons produces bond polarity.
rubric.description: Links a difference in electronegativity to bond polarity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that unequal electronegativities make a bond polar.

rubric.why: A larger electronegativity difference produces greater charge separation.
rubric.description: States how the size of the electronegativity difference affects polarity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that greater difference means greater polarity, or that equal electronegativities give a non-polar bond.

modelAnswer: A difference in electronegativity between bonded atoms makes the bond polar.
The greater the difference in electronegativity, the more polar the bond.

items.followUp: What is a triple covalent bond? Give one example.

rubric.why: A double covalent bond consists of two shared electron pairs.
rubric.description: Defines a double covalent bond in terms of shared electron pairs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that two pairs of electrons are shared between the atoms.

rubric.why: A valid molecule containing a double covalent bond is required as an example.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example of a double covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an appropriate example such as O₂.

modelAnswer: A double covalent bond is formed when two pairs of electrons are shared between two atoms.

items.followUp: Why can evaporation take place even when a liquid is below its boiling point?

rubric.why: Evaporation occurs at the exposed surface of a liquid.
rubric.description: Identifies molecules at the liquid surface as those that evaporate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning surface molecules.

rubric.why: At any temperature, some surface molecules have enough kinetic energy to escape into the air.
rubric.description: Explains why evaporation can continue below the boiling point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that energetic surface molecules escape continuously.

modelAnswer: Evaporation is continuous because some molecules at the liquid surface always have sufficient kinetic energy to escape into the air.
It can therefore occur at any temperature, including below the boiling point.
